newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metal industry welcomes Australia labour deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metal industry welcomes Australia labour deal.

text.p: The Metal Trades Industry Association of Australia said on Monday the government's labour reforms deal would give Australia an opportunity to introduce a more practical industrial relations system.
Chief executive Bob Herbert said the legislation would open up new options for companies and employees in the way they negotiated employment contracts.
"(But) it is important for all of us to remember that the proposed legislation is not a miracle panacea with all the benefits flowing tomorrow," Herbert said in a statement.
"Rather, the real worth of the legislation will come over time, when all the options it opens up are fully assessed and being utilised."
Herbert said one of the most important reforms would be the rationalisation and simplification of the current award system.
"It would be feasible under the new legislation to establish one common award base for all employees in manufacturing," he said.

Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith announced on Sunday the government had secured the passage of its Workplace Relations bill through an agreement with the Australian Democrats, under which 171 amendments would be made to the legislation.
The conservative Liberal-National coalition government needs minority support to get its legislation through the upper house of Parliament, the Senate, where it does not have a majority.
